question: A product list keeps `category` in a Zustand store initialized from the URL and written back in an effect. Users report that the back button changes the URL but not the list. What is the architectural fix?
options: Add a second effect that copies the URL into the store on every location change
Remove the store copy: derive `category` from the parsed search params during render and write it through navigation
Persist the store to `localStorage` so it survives navigation
Disable the back button on that screen
explanation: Two copies need syncing in both directions, and every missed path is a bug. With the URL as the only copy, back/forward, reload and deep links all read the same source.

question: `?sort=price&page=1` and `?page=1&sort=price` and `?sort=price` render the same results. Why serialize all of them as `?sort=price`?
options: Browsers reject query strings with default values
React Router cannot parse keys in a different order
Equal views then share one cache entry (CDN, browser, query keys) and one indexed URL instead of several duplicates
Shorter URLs make the JavaScript bundle smaller
explanation: Caches and search engines key on the exact string. Omitting defaults and sorting keys gives one canonical URL per view, which raises cache hits and avoids duplicate content.

question: Which history mode fits each write: typing in a search box, choosing a sort order, correcting an invalid `page=-3` link to the canonical URL?
options: Replace, push, replace
Push, push, push
Replace, replace, push
Push, replace, push
explanation: Continuous input and corrections the user did not ask for replace the entry; deliberate, discrete choices push so the back button can undo them.

question: An old marketing email links to `?sort=popularity`, a value removed last year. What should the screen's search schema do?
options: Throw so the error boundary shows a 404
Keep the unknown value and let the sort function ignore it
Redirect to the home page
Fall back to the default sort, so the link still opens a valid view (optionally replacing it with the canonical URL)
explanation: Links outlive releases. Validation with a fallback per field keeps old and hand-edited links working while the rest of the screen only sees valid, typed values.

question: Where should the rule "changing a filter resets the page to 1" live?
options: In every filter control's change handler
In the shared search-state hook (or schema), so every screen with pagination gets it
In the backend, which should ignore `page` when filters change
Nowhere: users can click Previous until results appear
explanation: It is a cross-cutting policy. Encoding it once next to the URL read/write logic prevents each screen from forgetting it and landing users on empty pages.
